# Best Practices for Citation-Backed Research Using Agentic AI

How a single human operator using an LLM-backed CLI agent can produce verifiable, auditable research documents. Originally synthesized from 37 sources (2026-03-29). **Updated 2026-04-19** with ~50 new sources (Q1-Q2 2026), full Discovery + Counter-Discovery pass across all 6 dimensions, cross-references to the concurrent `../agentic-research-bias/` 2026-04-18 update, and a retraction log for one materially corrected claim.

## Key Finding

Agentic research works not because agents are reliable, but because the methodology makes unreliability visible. Hallucination rates of 3-69% [8][15][30] become manageable when writer and verifier roles are structurally separated (with cross-family separation being the operative requirement per [54]), every claim is citation-linked, and an independent audit checks every source. The 2026-04-19 update sharpens two findings:

1. **Multi-agent debate alone does not improve expected correctness** — a NeurIPS 2025 martingale proof [42] shows debate reduces to majority voting on 7 benchmarks. Under equal thinking token budgets, single-agent systems match or outperform multi-agent on multi-hop reasoning [39][40].
2. **Citation hallucination has reached venue-level crisis** — ~300 ACL/NAACL/EMNLP 2024-25 papers contain hallucinated refs [50], 3-13% of deep-research-agent URLs are fabricated [49], and 57% of RAG citations lack faithfulness despite being correct [51].

## Decision Framework

1. **Use 3-5 parallel agents** for independently-decomposable research dimensions — but know the gain is primarily ensemble/voting, not agent-to-agent "debate" [42][43]. Under equal compute, single-agent may suffice [39][40].
2. **Require inline citations** in all agent output — forces the "dual-error" structural constraint [35]. Test both **correctness AND faithfulness** — 57% of correct citations are post-rationalized rather than causally grounded [51].
3. **Separate writer and verifier roles — across model families** — same-family verification has near-zero gain; cross-family works [54]. A 770M cross-family verifier can match GPT-4 fact-checking at 400× lower cost [12].
4. **Plan for 20-30% source inaccessibility** — provide 2-3 candidate sources per data point; tool choice matters (MCP success rates range 23-100% per counter-discovery scan). BuzzStream data [59] shows blocking doesn't prevent 70-92% of citations anyway.
5. **Gate irreversible decisions only** — plan approval, cross-source synthesis review, and final publication need human review. Source discovery and data extraction can proceed autonomously. Active modification (not just approval) preserves operator reasoning capacity [71].
6. **Avoid expert persona prompts for factual recall tasks** [14]; consider multi-persona for alignment/synthesis tasks [65]. Don't rely on CoT as audit trail — models disclose hint use in final answers only ~28.6% of the time [64].
7. **Use multi-agent Reflexion, not single-agent** — single-agent produces "degeneration of thought" via confirmation bias [70].

## Methodology

Original: 6 discovery agents dispatched in parallel (one per dimension), URL manifests aggregated, sources batch-fetched, 6 reference files and citations.md written, deliverable composed, two independent verification agents audited. Produced 2026-03-29.

Updated 2026-04-19: full re-discovery across all 6 dimensions (6 Discovery + 6 Counter-Discovery agents in parallel, model=sonnet, WebSearch-only, explicit no-Skill instruction). 19 new high-impact sources directly fetched; ~30 additional sources enter with explicit access qualifiers. One citation materially corrected (PaperBench 1.8% → 21% via [retraction-log.md](retraction-log.md)). Produced using the same cited-research methodology — which means this document is subject to every limitation it describes, including the newly-documented 42% turn-level autocorrelation caveat [87].
